# Speech and audio language-model foundations

<!-- Generated by scripts/catalog.py from data/models.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

[← Model index](../README.md#models)

**Reviewed as of 2026-09-12 · 35 entries.**

Textless speech LMs, joint speech-text pretraining, continuation models and general audio-generation foundations. These are not necessarily instruction-following assistants.

**Modalities:** T = text, I = image, V = video, A = general audio, S = speech, M = music, X = other structured modalities. A is a broad label, not a guarantee of every audio task. See the [methodology](../docs/methodology.md) for interaction labels, variant scope and inclusion rules.

Dates below refer to the linked paper or announcement, **not necessarily a weights/API release**. An em dash means no date was established from the reviewed source.

## Model notes

<a id="audiolm"></a>

### AudioLM

Continuation from an audio prompt; speech and music are demonstrated.

<a id="audiopalm"></a>

### AudioPaLM

Speech recognition and speech-to-speech translation built from text and audio language models.

<a id="calm"></a>

### CALM

Continuous Audio Language Models avoid discrete codec-token prediction; Pocket TTS is a later application.

<a id="dgslm"></a>

### dGSLM

Models two-speaker conversation continuations without text supervision.

<a id="flow-slm"></a>

### Flow-SLM

Jointly models linguistic content and acoustic context; distinct from Flow-Omni.

<a id="gemini-3-5-live-translate"></a>

### Gemini 3.5 Live Translate

Produces translated speech and transcripts from incoming speech.

**Listed variants:** gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview.

<a id="gpst"></a>

### GPST

Joint semantic and acoustic token generation for speech continuation.

<a id="gpt-realtime-translate"></a>

### GPT-Realtime-Translate

Speech translation while input is arriving; distinct from a general dialogue assistant.

**Listed variants:** gpt-realtime-translate.

<a id="gslm"></a>

### GSLM

Foundational textless language modeling and resynthesis from raw speech.

<a id="hibiki"></a>

### Hibiki

Processes source and target speech synchronously with aligned text; the original report evaluates French-to-English translation.

<a id="lauragpt"></a>

### LauraGPT

Unifies speech recognition, translation, enhancement and generation tasks.

<a id="mslam"></a>

### mSLAM

Multilingual speech-text representation model included as a foundation, rather than a spoken assistant.

<a id="parrot-ntpp"></a>

### Parrot / NTPP

Models dual-channel spoken dialogue; Parrot is the earlier workshop presentation.

**Listed variants:** Parrot; NTPP.

<a id="pgslm"></a>

### pGSLM

Extends textless speech generation with prosodic information.

<a id="seamlessexpressive"></a>

### SeamlessExpressive

Preserves prosody and vocal style across translated speech; not a general assistant.

<a id="seamlessm4t"></a>

### SeamlessM4T

Joint speech/text recognition and translation; included in broad speech-text foundations, not as a chat-tuned LLM.

**Listed variants:** Medium; Large.

<a id="seamlessm4t-v2"></a>

### SeamlessM4T v2

Updated multilingual speech/text translation model.

**Listed variants:** v2 Large.

<a id="seamlessstreaming"></a>

### SeamlessStreaming

Simultaneous multilingual translation with controlled input/output timing.

<a id="seed-liveinterpret-2-0"></a>

### Seed-LiveInterpret 2.0

Simultaneous speech translation with preservation of speaker characteristics.

**Listed variants:** 2.0.

<a id="soundstorm"></a>

### SoundStorm

Efficient conditional acoustic generation; a generation component rather than a conversational assistant.

<a id="speechgpt-gen"></a>

### SpeechGPT-Gen

Separates semantic prediction from acoustic-detail generation.

<a id="speechlm-synthetic-interleaved-pretraining"></a>

### SpeechLM (synthetic interleaved pretraining)

Named by its paper to distinguish this training study from the generic SpeechLM category.

**Listed variants:** Pretrained model; spoken-chat fine-tune.

<a id="speecht5"></a>

### SpeechT5

Unified speech/text pretraining for recognition, synthesis and conversion.

<a id="speechut"></a>

### SpeechUT

Bridges a speech encoder and text decoder through hidden units; evaluated on recognition and speech translation.

**Listed variants:** Base; Large.

<a id="speechx"></a>

### SpeechX

One model supports synthesis, editing, enhancement and other speech transformations.

<a id="spirit-lm"></a>

### Spirit LM

Base uses semantic units; Expressive adds pitch and style representations.

**Listed variants:** Base; Expressive.

<a id="sutlm"></a>

### SUTLM

Studies how to mix speech units and written text in one language model.

<a id="syllablelm"></a>

### SyllableLM

Uses syllable-scale units for textless speech modeling.

<a id="tada"></a>

### TADA

Aligns one continuous acoustic representation per text token; released pretraining targets continuation, not assistant dialogue.

**Listed variants:** 1B; 3B multilingual.

<a id="tgslm"></a>

### tGSLM

Textless language modeling with longer continuous units.

<a id="twist"></a>

### TWIST

Transfers pretrained text-model weights to spoken token sequences.

**Listed variants:** 1.3B; 7B; 13B.

<a id="uniaudio"></a>

### UniAudio

Universal audio generation covering speech, sounds, music and singing.

<a id="unity"></a>

### UnitY

Predicts target text before generating target speech units for speech translation.

<a id="viola"></a>

### VioLA

Unifies recognition, synthesis, translation and speech/text conversion.

<a id="voxtlm"></a>

### VoxtLM

Speech recognition/synthesis plus speech and text continuation.
